operation: Thiazol-5-ylmethyl unit (thiazole-5-carbaldehyde or a 5-(halomethyl)thiazole) as the N-substituent donor
shows: PN6047 carries a thiazol-5-ylmethyl group on the piperidine nitrogen; the same group is installed from 1,3-thiazole-5-carbaldehyde in WO2016/099393 Example Ib. Thiazoles are a recurrent ring in approved drugs, and ritonavir carries a thiazol-5-ylmethyl carbamate.
uncertainty: Supply, quality and registered-starting-material status of the thiazole building block are not documented in the sources examined. The tetrahydrobenzothiazole-2,6-diamine core of pramipexole is not a substructure of PN6047 and is not used as a fragment here.

operation: Construction of the N-Boc diarylmethylidene-piperidine core by Suzuki-Miyaura coupling of a vinyl bromide
status: Established (public record, milligram to gram scale)
shows: WO2016/099393 Example IV couples tert-butyl 4-{bromo[4-(dimethylcarbamoyl)phenyl]methylidene}piperidine-1-carboxylate (0.533 g) with (3-carbamoylphenyl)boronic acid using PdCl2(dppf) in DME/aqueous K2CO3 at 80 C. Wei et al. 2000 report two general approaches to this scaffold class: dehydration of benzhydryl alcohols and Suzuki coupling of vinyl bromides. Qian et al. 2010 report a continuous-flow synthesis of a close analogue.
uncertainty: No yield, impurity profile or palladium level is reported for the PN6047 coupling in the text examined (crude product taken on). The preparation of the vinyl bromide is not described in the portion examined.

operation: Large-scale palladium-catalysed couplings and removal of residual palladium
shows: Large-scale applications of Pd couplings in pharmaceutical synthesis are reviewed; methods for removing palladium from APIs have been reviewed and silica-based scavengers described; ICH Q3D sets a Class 2B oral PDE of 100 ug/day for Pd.
uncertainty: Whether the PN6047 core (two amides, a basic piperidine) allows effective Pd purge by scavenging or crystallisation is substrate-specific and untested here.

shows: WO2016/099393 Example III uses HATU (1.15 g), DIPEA and dimethylamine hydrochloride in DMF. Amide coupling reagents used at scale are reviewed by Dunetz et al. 2016. The HOAt/HOBt unit in such reagents is associated with explosive properties of 1-hydroxybenzotriazoles (Wehrstedt et al. 2005).
uncertainty: The starting material named in the machine-readable text of Example III is not the compound required by Example IV; only the reagent class is used here. In R1/R2 the amide is pre-installed in a purchased aryl building block, which moves the question to that building block's availability.

operation: Boc removal and isolation of the secondary amine
shows: WO2016/099393 Example V removes the Boc group with trifluoroacetic acid in dichloromethane (0.630 g). Boc removal with acids is a standard protecting-group operation (Isidro-Llobet et al. 2009).
uncertainty: Isolation of the amine as a crystalline hydrochloride from a Class 3 solvent (R1) is a change of conditions for this substrate (condition evidence C).

operation: N-functionalisation by reductive amination with NaBH(OAc)3
shows: WO2016/099393 Example Ib: 40 mg of the secondary amine and 1,3-thiazole-5-carbaldehyde, AcOH, NaBH(OAc)3, 1,2-dichloroethane, rt, 2 days; preparative HPLC; 8.2 mg (16 %). Abdel-Magid et al. 1996 describe the reagent and name DCE as the preferred solvent, with THF and occasionally acetonitrile as alternatives.
uncertainty: 1,2-dichloroethane is an ICH Q3C Class 1 solvent. A change to THF or acetonitrile has general precedent (B/C) but has not been shown for this substrate; an ester solvent would be a hypothesis. Conversion, over-reduction and impurity formation at scale are unknown.

operation: Crystalline hydrochloride salt as the isolated form
status: Established (public record, forms described; no scale reported)
shows: WO2022/013153 describes crystalline Forms HCl2 and HCl3 of the PN6047 hydrochloride, Form HCl2 from solvents including 2-propanol, acetone, acetonitrile, ethanol, ethyl acetate or tetrahydrofuran, with improved stability and low hygroscopicity relative to amorphous material; the amorphous salt was made on a 500.5 mg scale by lyophilisation from TFE/water and dried at 80 C for 3 days. Salt-selection practice is reviewed by Bastin et al. 2000.
uncertainty: Crystallisation as the main impurity-purging step (replacing preparative HPLC) is not demonstrated in the sources examined.

operation: Process handover from discovery to development
shows: Federsel 2009 discusses the transfer of chemistry from medicinal chemistry to process R&D and the technical, safety and scalability questions that arise. Carey et al. 2006 survey the chemistries used in process R&D at three companies. Brown and Bostrom 2016 find amide formation and Suzuki-Miyaura coupling among the most frequently used reactions in medicinal chemistry.
uncertainty: None of these sources concerns PN6047; they support the general premise that a discovery-scale route is not by itself a manufacturing route.
